quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: The traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light at an intersection, slow down and stop before entering if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Signal the lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal first, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see all traffic around your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must and must not do. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to scare them so they won't cross against the red light again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if you have a green light. Pedestrian safety comes first. Be careful around pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when it rains because visibility is reduced. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the side of the road and stop until it improves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign warns you to slow down when approaching an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers or pedestrians go first. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: Traffic lights sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is only used on one-way streets.
You may go, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
You may only proceed if there is also a circular green light.
It points to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you have a protected turn. You may proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights or gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger signals you, when you see a stop sign, or when there are flashing lights or gates. Some crossings do not have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. Wait to drive when you feel emotionally stable.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Use extra force to steer, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use extra force to steer, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you will need extra effort to steer. Reduce your speed and move off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: Why should you signal before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb?

options.text: Only if other vehicles are near.
It is good practice and required by law.
Only during the move, not before.
Not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is good practice and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle right or left. Always signal before leaving a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because few vehicles are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
When there is a solid yellow line next to you and the passing lane is clear.
None of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of these.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass by crossing a solid yellow line.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns of hazards or danger.
It alerts you to school zones.
It alerts you to recreation areas.
It alerts you to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns of hazards or danger.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about existing or possible hazards. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging.
Multiple turns ahead.
Lane is shifting.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They get you ready for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the roadside with nobody inside.
When it approaches you, even without flashing lights.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What should you do when you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them to retaliate.
Show them you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if a driver is threatening or driving dangerously near you. Try to increase the distance between you. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make gestures.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your blood alcohol level is to wait. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your level or reduce alcohol's effects. They may help you stay awake, but they cannot change your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medications can affect your driving ability. Check the label for warnings about side effects. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about driving while taking a medication.

questions.question: Which is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you decrease your speed, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less well your tires grip the surface. If you drive too fast, your tires will lose contact with the road and you will hydroplane (slide on a film of water).

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left at a green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You may complete your turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver under 21 with a probationary license:

options.text: May use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
May not drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
Should not wear a seat belt while driving.
May use a hand-held cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Drivers with probationary licenses have restrictions. They cannot use any cell phone (hand-held or hands-free) and must wear a seat belt. Drivers under 21 cannot operate a vehicle between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your vehicle will take longer to stop on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which of the following affects how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All three choices
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Eating slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment from too much alcohol.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to break the laws because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
Will have their bicycle impounded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both motorists and bicyclists who break traffic laws can be ticketed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: U-turns are prohibited.
U-turns are permitted.
Winding road ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are prohibited.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means an action is not allowed. U-turns are not permitted where this sign is posted.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Maintain your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking hard and carefully steer back onto the pavement. Check for nearby traffic before re-entering the road.

questions.question: When you are being tailgated:

options.text: Move over to the right if there is an open lane.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to encourage the tailgater to pass you.
Never slow down abruptly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated and a right lane is available, move to the right. If not, wait until it is safe ahead, then slowly reduce speed to let the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly because this increases the risk of a rear-end collision.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risks of crashes caused by alcohol?

options.text: Decide before you drink that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you have started drinking.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you don't leave your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can also be unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle has flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid crashes.
Getting ahead of bad drivers to protect yourself from them.
Following the car ahead of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations early and act to prevent crashes. It helps protect you from reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass when they have flashing lights or a siren on.

questions.question: When should you leave more space than usual in front of your car?

options.text: When stopped on a hill.
When stopped at an intersection.
When stopped at a stop sign.
When stopped at a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopped on a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped uphill. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts, you are less likely to crash.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on a public road or sidewalk. This applies to all passengers and locations in the vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are allowed.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means an action is not allowed. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your car?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your car on all sides so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to cars next to you.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop at any red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: You must use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means a pedestrian is blind. You must slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than the flow of traffic.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Always drive with the flow of traffic and obey the speed limit.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, you should:

options.text: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right lane only when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is ahead and you should slow down.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Red means stop. You must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian signals for you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against the light or are being careless.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You may drive around railroad crossing gates:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Under no circumstances.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never go around a lowered railroad gate. Stop whenever you see flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or hear a train whistle. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest side and stop.
